SPECIFICATION FOR 
FASTENER, PAPER, PRONG TYPE, WITH WASHER 



1. Scope — The materials, dimensions and performance requirements for round head, prong 
type fastener with washer used for holding the sheets of paper together and for use with file 
folders-

3. Material 

3.1 The prongs, head and the washer shall be made of the same material and may be of brass or 
steel or aluminium of suitable type and grade. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The fastener shall be made from two pieces. The width and thickness of the two pieces shall 
conform to Table 1. The prong shall be bent back on itself to form a head at right angles. The 
head piece shall be a circular disc and crimped over the flat head of the prong piece. The diameter 
of the head shall be as specified in Table 1. One prong shall be shorter than the other by not less 
than V6 mm nor more than 3'2 mm. The longer prong end shall have a V-shaped point. The 
shorter prong end shall have either a rounded or V-shaped point. 



4.2 The washer shall be round in shape, 
the fastener for which they are intended. 
Table 1. 



The slot shall be of sufficient size to take the prongs of

4.3 The fastener and washer shall be clean and free from defects which may effect appearance and 
serviceability. 

4.4 The fastener and the washer shall be free from burrs, sharp edges or corners that might be 
hazardous to the user. 

4.5 The fastener and the washer if required by the purchaser shall be nickel or chromium coated, if 
made of steel, conforming to Grade 3 of 13:1068-1968 'Electroplated coatings of nickel and 
chromium on iron and steel (first revision ) \ 

4.6 The fastener and the washer if required by the purchaser shall be anodized, if made of 
aluminium, conforming to IS : 1868-1968 * Aaodic coatings on aluminium (first revision) \ 

AJl The fastener and the washer if required by the purchaser shall be plated chromium over nickel, 
if made of brass, conforming to Grade 3 of 18:4827-1968 * Electroplated coatings of nickel and 
chromium on copper and copper alloys '. 

5. Tests 

5.1 Performance — Slowly spread the prongs of the fasteners to the position they would assume In 
actual use in fastening papers together. Slowly press the prongs back between the fingers until they 
reach their original position. This shall constitute one bend. Repeat the test for 25 times. Examinefor 
cracking, breaking and loosening of the prongs inside the head of the fastener. The fastener shall 
be free from the defects. 

5.2 Corrosion Resistance — Dip the fasteners with washers in a solution of mineral spirit to remove 
ihe surface film or grease and wipe dry. Place the specimen in a boiling 10 percent ( by weight ) 
aqueous solution of sodium chloride for 15 minutes. Remove the specimens from the solution at 
room temperature. Allow to dry at room temperature. At the end of the test examine the specimens 
1or signs of corrosion. There shall not be any corrosion visible on the specimen. 

5.3 Flexibility — The prongs of the fastener shall be folded five times on its own thickness. They 
shall not show any sign of damage or crack after the test. 

'6. Marking 

6.1 Each packet containing the fasteners and the washers shall be clearly and indelibly marked with 
the manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark and size. 

€.2 iSI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing —The fasteners and the washers shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier.
